newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea rescues North Korean aboard drifting boat.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea rescues North Korean aboard drifting boat.

text.p: South Korea on Saturday rescued a North Korean man aboard a small boat drifting off a South Korean island, the Maritime Police Agency said.

A police statement said the steel boat drifted south from North Korea while the man on board tried to repair its engine. Maritime police first spotted the boat on Friday about 21 miles southwest of South Korea's So Yonpyongdo island, which is close to the border with the communist North, it said.
The North Korean on board the boat, identified as Chung Kwang-son, 19, initially refused help from South Korean rescuers but later accepted a police offer of help, a police officer said.
The statement said Chung was being questioned by military investigators but gave no details.
The domestic Yonhap news agency, quoting investigators, said Chung was a navy diver but the police officer could not confirm the report.

Tense relations between the two Koreas have worsened since a North Korean submarine landed 26 agents on a South Korean beach in September. Twenty-four of them were shot dead, one was captured alive and another is still at large.
